sections.title: Project and products
sections.prompt: What is this project, which products belong to it, and what is outside its scope? Keep exact names, IDs, owners and current or intended availability.

sections.title: Customers and value
sections.prompt: Who uses, buys or benefits from the offer? Describe their situation, problem and the value currently delivered or intended.

sections.title: Current state
sections.prompt: What exists or has been observed? Attribute supplied statements, tested work, results and assets; distinguish them from intentions.

sections.title: Business and resources
sections.prompt: What is known about channels, delivery, prices, revenue, funding, people, partners, costs and capacity? State units, sources and constraints.

sections.title: Goals and success
sections.prompt: What does the owner want to achieve, with which priorities, baseline, target and time horizon where supplied?

sections.title: Visual reference intake
sections.prompt: Record identity and references for interface and website, typography, photography, illustration and marketing creative. Attach exact files and record preferences, rights and review state.

sections.title: Strategic direction
sections.prompt: Describe the intended marketing system, positioning and durable trade-offs that fulfill the reviewed Brief.

sections.title: Audiences and product roles
sections.prompt: Which audiences and situations matter, what value does each confirmed product deliver, and what behavior should it support?

sections.title: Growth system
sections.prompt: How do prioritized channels work together? Give each a role, audience, content or value, destination and growth mechanism.

sections.title: Customer journey
sections.prompt: Describe discovery, useful value, purchase or adoption, continued use and recommendations from the customer's perspective.

sections.title: Measurement and priorities
sections.prompt: Connect outcomes to observable signals and management decisions. State resource priorities and risks that could change the direction.

sections.title: Brand identity
sections.prompt: What are the exact public brand and product names, their relationship, naming rules and optional slogan?

sections.title: Intended perception
sections.prompt: What should the audience understand, trust and remember? Describe character, difference and impressions to avoid.

sections.title: Meaning and message hierarchy
sections.prompt: Connect the audience's situation to the promise, supporting proof, objections and next action.

sections.title: Voice and language
sections.prompt: Define terminology, tone, sentence and evidence rules, with examples of suitable and unsuitable wording.

sections.title: Consistency rules
sections.prompt: Which naming, promise, evidence, commercial and support rules must hold across products and channels?

sections.title: Design intent
sections.prompt: Describe the reviewed visual preferences, brand character, reusable graphic language and do/do-not rules. Keep all five taste categories distinct.

sections.title: Identity application
sections.prompt: Describe how the approved name and identity assets appear in lockups and different contexts. Attach real sources.

sections.title: Visual system
sections.prompt: Define semantic colors, typography, weights, languages, licenses, fallbacks and their usage.

sections.title: Iconography
sections.prompt: Name the library, version, source and license, or the custom drawing method. Specify the family, states, labels and actual glyph examples.

sections.title: Interface and product surfaces
sections.prompt: Define reusable layout, components, interaction states, accessibility and responsive principles. Product-specific pages belong to that product.

sections.title: Photography
sections.prompt: Define purpose, evidence limits, style prompt, production specification, example assets and the review gate. Preserve masters and prepare square deliveries separately.

sections.title: Illustration and diagrams
sections.prompt: Define purpose, evidence limits, style prompt, production specification, example assets and the review gate for illustrations and diagrams.

sections.title: Outputs and provenance
sections.prompt: Identify actual supplied and generated assets, originals and deliveries, prompts, tools, rights, review and permitted use.

sections.title: Products
sections.prompt: List every confirmed product with a stable ID, name, summary and its own document. Retain drafts and products outside the current priority.

sections.title: Product identity
sections.prompt: State the brand, product name, category, lifecycle, owner and boundary.

sections.title: Customer Segments
sections.prompt: Distinguish user, buyer, payer, beneficiary and decision-maker. Give segments stable IDs, qualifying situations, triggers and exclusions.

sections.title: Problem and desired progress
sections.prompt: Describe the customer's circumstance, desired progress, functional, social and emotional forces, pains and gains.

sections.title: Value Propositions
sections.prompt: Compare actual alternatives, differentiated capabilities and the customer value they enable. Link the offer to jobs, pains and gains.

sections.title: Offer and usage
sections.prompt: Define access or deliverable unit, included and excluded scope, experience, support, rights and dependencies.

sections.title: Revenue Streams
sections.prompt: For each segment state payer, unit, price or pricing rule, currency, cadence, payment timing and conditions. For a free offer record the intended non-cash exchange separately from money revenue.

sections.title: Key Activities
sections.prompt: Which work creates and delivers the value, and who owns it? Reference the Sales process without duplicating it.

sections.title: Key Resources
sections.prompt: Identify people, infrastructure, finance and intellectual resources, owners, availability and constraints. Record this product's share and allocation basis for shared resources.

sections.title: Key Partnerships
sections.prompt: Which suppliers and partners contribute, what do they do, and which dependencies or agreements have evidence?

sections.title: Cost Structure
sections.prompt: Describe fixed and variable costs, amount, currency, period and calculation basis. Separate cash from founder time and state shared allocations. Include Funding: capital or subsidy provider, conditions and limits, separately from customer revenue.

sections.title: Assumptions and decision rules
sections.prompt: Give material assumptions stable IDs, sources and states, with signals and consequences for the affected decisions. Link the Research that tests them.

sections.title: Business goals and metrics
sections.prompt: Connect acquisition, customer value, adoption, revenue and continued use to relevant business signals and management decisions. Give numerical targets a basis.

sections.title: Sales
sections.prompt: Describe the complete customer process for each segment: discovery, evaluation, purchase or adoption, delivery, use, help and continued use. Reference the Product's money terms.

sections.title: Promotion
sections.prompt: Describe this product's Website, Marketing Creative and Presentation where relevant, applying the reviewed Strategy, Brand and Design.

sections.title: Analytics & Research
sections.prompt: Keep measured results, source and time window separate from research findings and hypotheses. Link findings to this Product's assumptions.
